s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain and constipation with a tender midline abdominal mass and history of amenorrhea
key_facts: Tender midline abdominal mass on physical examination
Negative point-of-care urine human chorionic gonadotropin test
Ultrasonography confirmed live intrauterine pregnancy at 24 weeks

raw.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain and constipation with a tender midline abdominal mass and history of amenorrhea
key_facts: Tender midline abdominal mass on physical examination

shortlist.label: Uterine leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Tender midline abdominal mass and history of amenorrhea

shortlist.label: Ovarian tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal pain and constipation with a history of amenorrhea

shortlist.label: Uterine sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Tender midline abdominal mass and history of amenorrhea

shortlist.label: Intra-abdominal fibromatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal pain and constipation with a tender midline abdominal mass

shortlist.label: Ovarian cystadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal pain and constipation with a history of amenorrhea

raw.rationale: The presence of a tender midline abdominal mass and the patient's symptoms of abdominal pain, constipation, and amenorrhea, along with the ultrasonography confirmation of a live intrauterine pregnancy, suggest a uterine leiomyoma (fibroid) as the most likely diagnosis. The high serum hCG level is consistent with a pregnancy complication, and uterine leiomyomas are known to be associated with pregnancy complications and can cause the symptoms described.

rejected.label: Ovarian tumor
rejected.why: While ovarian tumors can cause abdominal pain and constipation, the presence of a live intrauterine pregnancy and a tender midline abdominal mass is more suggestive of a uterine rather than ovarian pathology.

rejected.label: Uterine sarcoma
rejected.why: Uterine sarcomas are rare and aggressive tumors, and the patient's presentation and test results do not strongly suggest this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Intra-abdominal fibromatosis
rejected.why: Intra-abdominal fibromatosis is a rare condition that typically presents with a palpable abdominal mass, but the patient's symptoms and test results are more consistent with a uterine rather than an intra-abdominal process.

rejected.label: Ovarian cystadenoma
rejected.why: Ovarian cystadenomas are typically benign tumors that can cause abdominal pain, but the patient's presentation and test results, including the presence of a live intrauterine pregnancy and a tender midline abdominal mass, are more suggestive of a uterine rather than ovarian pathology.
